conviction_note: Net income almost certainly fell sharply quarter on quarter. The BBVA parent's 3Q26 segment report has Argentina at EUR29m against EUR46m in 2Q26, Goldman forecasts -27% real and Citi is 6% under consensus, so the headline should miss a stale consensus of roughly ARS130bn by about 20-25%. Three things soften that: the miss was published a month ago, asset quality is confirmed to have turned, and the stock already fell 22.8% in 20 days with its sector to near its 52-week low. The sum of the findings (-1.1) and the scaled number (p_up 45 x 5.0 = -0.5) agree in sign; the scaled number is smaller because the next session is likely dominated by Argentina macro and GGAL's print on the same evening.

next_guide.company_current_guide: From the 2Q26 call on 2026-08-28: FY2026 real ROE in the low teens, about 10% real loan growth, deposits +5-10%, cost of risk about 6.5%, NPL about 5.5% at year-end, efficiency below 45%, inflation about 29%, historical NIM down about 200bp by year-end (https://www.webull.com/news/15497683419390976).
next_guide.basis: The year-to-date arithmetic does not reach the guide. Quarterly ROE was 8.3% in Q1 and 12.2% in Q2, and Goldman has Q3 at 8.8%, so low teens for the year needs a Q4 near 20%. The parent's report shows cost of risk at 7.52% year to date against the 6.5% guide, and lending up 23.4% in 9M against 23.6% inflation, roughly flat in real terms against a 10% real guide. findings.finding: BBVA Group's 3Q26 business-area report, published 2026-10-29, shows Argentina's net attributable profit at EUR29m in 3Q26 against EUR46m in 2Q26 (1H26 EUR73m, 9M26 EUR102m), down about 37% in euros. It attributes the fall to 'lower recurring revenue and NTI, partially offset by a lower negative adjustment for hyperinflation'. Against a consensus of about ARS132bn, flat on 2Q26's ARS131.6bn, that implies a headline net-income miss of roughly 20-30%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2Q26's +44.6% QoQ profit and 25.7% EPS beat drew -0.9% the next day (2026-08-28). 1Q26's -21% YoY profit drew +5.1% (2026-05-27). The stock has not traded consistently on the headline line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced. Goldman already forecasts -27% real QoQ, and the stock fell 22.8% over 20 days, though with its sector. The published consensus (Citi's '6% below consensus', FXEmpire's ARS128bn, Investing's ARS144bn) still sits near flat QoQ, so the aggregated bar has not absorbed the parent's disclosure. If it had, consensus would read about ARS95-105bn. Caveats: the group figure is 66.55% attributable, under full IFRS and group adjustments, and translated at period-end rates, so the local decline could be smaller than the euro decline.
findings.independence: Goldman's -27% real QoQ forecast and ROE of 8.8% (https://www.iprofesional.com/finanzas/468851-wall-street-recomienda-una-sola-accion-entre-los-bancos-argentinos), and Citi at ARS124.49bn. Supervielle's 3Q26 NII fell 22.4% QoQ on the same rate mechanics (https://www.riotimesonline.com/grupo-supervielle-q3-earnings-2026/).

findings.finding: The same parent report shows asset quality turning in 3Q26. Argentina's NPL ratio was 6.0% at 30 Sep 2026, down 39bp in the quarter, and year-to-date cost of risk was 7.52%, down 19bp. NPL inflows were lower, recoveries higher and write-offs higher; coverage slipped to 76%. This confirms the 2Q26 call's statement that Q2 was the peak for NPLs and cost of risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In 2Q26 NPL rose from 5.60% to 6.09% and coverage fell from 88% to 80% while the stock moved -0.9%. No clean record of the stock trading on an asset-quality improvement.
findings.why_not_priced: The sector sold off through November on macro (country risk 745 to 830-940), not on credit data. Goldman's NPL forecast of 5.9% is close to this, so it is partly in the bar. If the improvement were priced, the bank ADRs would not sit near 52-week lows with Goldman citing credit and capital concerns. Higher write-offs flatter the ratio and coverage is lower, so the improvement is real but of mixed quality.
findings.independence: BCRA August 2026 bank report: system private NPL flat at 7.75% for four months and households slightly lower at 12.81% (https://www.bcra.gob.ar/publicaciones/informe-sobre-bancos-agosto-de-2026/). BCRA says the household irregular stock has fallen since August (https://www.forbesargentina.com/money/la-mora-bancaria-empieza-bajar-banco-central-ya-habla-fin-ciclo-atrasos-n101351). Shares a document with the previous finding, but a different line.

findings.finding: Peer Grupo Supervielle reported 3Q26 on 2026-11-16. NIM fell to 16.0% from 20.3% and NII fell 22.4% QoQ because the 2Q gap between falling market rates and slower deposit-rate cuts closed, and because lower inflation cut CER/UVA income. It cut its 2026 real loan-growth guide to 0-5% from 10-15% and its ROE guide to 5-6% from 8-10%, and missed EPS consensus at $0.08 against $0.16. BBAR's NIM was 18.2% in 2Q26, with peso NIM at 21.8%.
findings.link: Same Argentine peso rate and inflation environment over the same quarter. Both are mid-to-large private banks with peso NIMs that benefited in 2Q26 from deposit-rate lag. BBAR guided its own NIM down about 100-200bp by year-end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BBAR's NIM moved from 18.6% to 18.2% in 2Q26 and the stock moved -0.9%. No record of the stock trading on NIM alone.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the print was public eight days before this one and Goldman models BBAR's NIM falling from 14.4% to 13%. Filed small as peer transmission.
findings.independence: Guidance table at https://finsee.ai/earnings/supv/2026/q3/en/. The parent report's 'lower recurring revenue' for BBVA Argentina points the same way.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide from the 2Q26 call (real ROE low teens, about 10% real loan growth, cost of risk about 6.5%) is out of reach on the year-to-date numbers, so a cut is likely. ROE was 8.3% in Q1 and 12.2% in Q2, with Q3 near 8.8% on Goldman's forecast. The parent's report shows cost of risk at 7.52% year to date and lending up 23.4% in 9M against 23.6% inflation. The NPL guide of about 5.5% at year-end is the one line on track.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced record of BBAR's reaction to a guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced. Goldman cut its 2026 earnings forecast by 18% and Supervielle cut across the board, so a cut is the base case. What is not known is its depth, and whether management resets 2027 (it guided system loan growth of 10-15% real for 2027). If the cut were fully priced, the street's Q4 estimate of $0.47 would sit below Q3's, not above it.
findings.independence: BBVA parent 3Q26 report (https://shareholdersandinvestors.bbva.com/informes/3q26-report-business-areas-south-america/) and Supervielle's guide cuts (https://finsee.ai/earnings/supv/2026/q3/en/).

baseline_tension: The baseline carries no skew; the 20-day run-up of -22.8% says the market has already marked the sector down hard. The evidence leans negative on the reported number but agrees with that drawdown, which already reflects much of it, so the lean is kept mild.
lessons_applied: Lesson 3 (one fact counted once): the price-path and targets finding went from +1.0 to +0.8. Goldman's forecast had already shrunk the first finding and was no longer counted again in the expectations finding.
Lesson 5 (proxy smaller): the Supervielle peer finding went from -0.5 to -0.4; the parent's company-level document carries the reported-quarter read.

Lesson 1 and the FPI history lesson: reaction history rebuilt from confirmed releases (2026-05-27 +5.1%, 2026-08-28 -0.9%) instead of the baseline's 6-K matches. The first finding stays at -1.5 rather than being sized larger, because this stock has not traded reliably on the headline line.
Lesson 6 (bar): the consensus is sourced only loosely (Citi's '6% below', FXEmpire, Investing, Benzinga), so no finding exceeds 1.5 points.
